subject: Bar chart for contingency table outcomes

messages.author: 62da3332a76a2586
messages.subject: Bar chart for contingency table outcomes
parts:
I appologize in advance for this simplistic question. I'm just
starting to learn R and work with ggplot.

I'm looking to generate a simple bar chart in ggplot comparing the %
experiencing an outcome who were exposed to the % experiencing an
outcome who were unexposed. A summary contingency table looks like
this:

Exposed 0 1
Outcome
0 215 184
1 58 93

I'm trying to create a bar chart with a scale of 0 to 100% with bar 1
showing outcome % among the exposed (93/184 or 51%) and bar 2 showing
the outcome % among the unexposed (58/215 or 27%).

I have been trying to work with the sample code for bar charts from
the ggplots website but none of the examples deal with % outcomes with
a discrete exposure variable. This code below is starting to get me
there, but it only shows outcome counts (58 and 93) and also provides
counts for the null outcome (215 and 184), which I'd like excluded:

d<- ggplot(dataset, aes(x=factor(outcome), fill=factor(exposed)))
> d+geom_bar(position="dodge")

Any suggestions?

Thanks very much!
Sam

On Aug 12, 12:52 pm, SMJ <smjenn...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I appologize in advance for this simplistic question. I'm just
> starting to learn R and work with ggplot.
>
> I'm looking to generate a simple bar chart in ggplot comparing the %
> experiencing an outcome who were exposed to the % experiencing an
> outcome who were unexposed. A summary contingency table looks like
> this:
>
>           Exposed 0   1
> Outcome
> 0                    215 184
> 1                     58  93
>
> I'm trying to create a bar chart with a scale of 0 to 100% with bar 1
> showing outcome % among the exposed (93/184 or 51%) and bar 2 showing
> the outcome % among the unexposed (58/215 or 27%).
>
> I have been trying to work with the sample code for bar charts from
> the ggplots website but none of the examples deal with % outcomes with
> a discrete exposure variable. This code below is starting to get me
> there, but it only shows outcome counts (58 and 93) and also provides
> counts for the null outcome (215 and 184), which I'd like excluded:
>
> d<- ggplot(dataset, aes(x=factor(outcome), fill=factor(exposed)))
>
> > d+geom_bar(position="dodge")
>
> Any suggestions?
>
> Thanks very much!
> Sam

Sam,

First, it helps to have a reproducible example, including data.
Having given the contingency table, it is not too hard to recreate the
data, though:

dataset <- data.frame(exposed = rep(c(0,1,0,1),
times=c(215,184,58,93)),
outcome = rep(c(0,1), times=c(215+184, 58+93)))

Typically, the way to do this is to use the "fill" position which
stacks things up and renormalizes them to 1 (100%).

ggplot(dataset, aes(x=factor(exposed), fill=factor(outcome))) +
geom_bar(position="fill")

Note that I switched the x and fill aesthetics; you want to "stack
up" (and normalize within) exposure groups, so that is your x. But
you said that you did not want to show the "0" outcome group, just the
"1". Were you to drop those 0's out of the data.frame and plot that,
they would also not be counted for purposes of normalization. The
only way to do this is to pre-summarize the data and just plot the
parts you want.

# create cross tabs
cts <- xtabs(~outcome+exposed, data=dataset)
# turn into proportions; the 2 indicates the "direction"
cts <- prop.table(cts,2)
# convert to data.frame (ggplot2 likes data.frames)
cts <- as.data.frame(cts)
# subset to only the outcome 1 part; must be done last because full
data needed for computing proportions.
cts <- cts[cts$outcome==1,]

# since pre-summarized, set y aesthetic and set position="identity"
ggplot(cts, aes(x=exposed, y=Freq)) +
geom_bar(position="identity")

--
Brian Diggs
Senior Research Associate, Oregon Health & Science University
